answers-lazy.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty of two thousand rows, abandoned, fifty times over. The inference pin is ZERO and that zero is the case: bridge.pl's metta_node_guarded/2 reports what a job spent as that job's LAST event, reached only once the command has no more answers, so an abandoned job contributes nothing. A lazy path that began draining would report query-rows' 282622 and fail this row by four orders of magnitude, and the workload's own crossing bound fails first at 1600. Instructions carry the SIZE, since a counter fixed at zero cannot say whether twenty rows cost twenty rows' work or two thousand; most of what they price is the teardown, because leaving the loop early closes the cursor and destroys the engine behind it. Fifty abandonments rather than one because a two millisecond window spread 0.2763 percent across nine samples against a one percent band. Inferences identical in all 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs; instructions spread 0.0399 percent over 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs [measured 2026-08-28: minimum of [815818054, 815831092, 815774521]; command=CHECK_PY=<an interpreter with janus_swi> sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build, box under loadavg 9 with another gate running; commit=0f6803e2377036ae526474434851b7a592f04703] RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 for a HARNESS fix, not a code change: every instruction row moved at once and every inference row stayed identical, which is the signature of the measurement rather than the work. benchmarks/sampler.ts now collects the heap to a fixed point at the end of setup, outside the window, under a fourth V8 flag `--expose-gc`. The three flags already there make a run reproducible against ITSELF; this makes it reproducible against a CHANGED PROGRAM. `--predictable-gc-schedule` is deterministic given the same allocation sequence and the startup heap is part of that sequence, so growing any module the benchmark loads shifted where a collection landed inside the window. Measured rather than argued, by a probe that cannot possibly do work: four kilobytes of INERT COMMENTS added to src/theory.ts moved host-op from 900018262 to 933434511, a 3.7 percent phantom regression from text nothing executes, and the same probe against the settled heap moves the whole suite at most 0.18 percent (atom-intern), with host-op at 0.016 percent. The rows that went UP now carry the collections their own allocation causes instead of inheriting an accidental share of the startup heap's, which is why answers-lazy and query-rows rose while host-op and atom-intern fell. This is the layout-bias class Mytkowicz et al. name, and a settled starting heap is the cheap half of Stabilizer's answer to it [source: Mytkowicz, Diwan, Hauswirth and Sweeney, "Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!", ASPLOS 2009; Curtsinger and Berger, "Stabilizer", ASPLOS 2013].
